notes:
**The name on your logo link is no longer mistaken for your company name.**

Docket reads four places to learn what a site calls itself, and one of them is
the accessible name of the logo link. That name describes where the link goes —
"NHS homepage", "archive home" — so Docket strips the navigation words off it
and keeps what is left. On a site whose logo link is named "archive home", what
was left was "archive", and the report said the company used two different
names, neither of which it uses.

A logo link's name is the weakest of the four sources: a description of a
destination, not a declaration of identity. What survives the stripping now has
to look like the site's own domain, which is the one piece of identity a site
cannot fake. Measured over six crawled sites, every real name still corroborates
— Navy Federal, UNISON, Basecamp — and only the navigation label does not.

The trade, stated plainly: a company on a domain that does not contain its name
loses this one source. Its `og:site_name` and Organization schema are
declarations of identity, still read in full, so a genuine disagreement between
what you declare and what your titles say is still reported.
